content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text decides a collision between the challenger's chain and the defender's chain using explicit-naming and inference concerns rather than weighing the chains solely by footing.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "none", "why": "Although it calls both chains footed, the judge's stated reasons fault the challenger for not explicitly naming Joseph and the defender for relying on an inference, which is the forbidden verse-by-verse/stating-verse inquiry rather than a chain-by-chain footing comparison."}
